newsitem.title: DUBAI: Study suggests $30 billion Gulf Arab rail network.
newsitem.headline: Study suggests $30 billion Gulf Arab rail network.

text.p: Gulf Arab states should set up a rail network to reduce transport costs and boost tourism, a study carried out by the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) said.
The study, released by the official Saudi Press Agency on Thursday, said the $30 billion project would cost the same as the current road and highway networks linking Gulf Arab states.
A rail link would be more efficient than road freight transport and would boost tourism in the area by encouraging more people to travel between the oil-rich countries, it said.
Annual costs of maintaining the region's vast road networks stand at $3 billion, the study added.
The GCC is a political and economic alliance comprising Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Bahrain, the United Arab Emirates, Qatar and Oman.
